alignments.note: The ASV supplies the subordinator *though* for a protasis whose Hebrew writes no conjunction at all — the verse opens with the bare numeral שְׁלֹשֶׁת. Rule 55: no morpheme licenses it, and it is not folded into the preposition or the demonstrative standing beside it.
Demonstrative pronoun takes the ASV's *these*.
Article on אֲנָשִׁים: the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase, and rule 41's limit gives the single determiner to the demonstrative morpheme that licenses it (rule 29).
Numeral in construct takes *three*; the ASV renders the chain attributively, so rule 19's relational word is not written (rule 28).
Head noun → *men*.
Second article, agreeing with the demonstrative; the ASV writes one determiner for the phrase (rules 41, 47).

CORRECTED. בְּתוֹךְ is rendered by the single English word *in*, so rule 30 fuses the preposition with its construct noun — the same terms as בְּיַד → *by* — headed on the lexeme-bearing תָּוֶךְ. The verbless clause's supplied copula *were* joins the prepositional predicate's unit, which rule 30 expressly allows for a fused expression (לִפְנֵי → *was before*) and rule 49 requires. The accepted reading gave *in* to בְּ alone and marked תָּוֶךְ `unrepresented`, which rule 30 rules out where the one-English-word condition is met.
Pronominal suffix realized by *it* (rule 18).

The oath formula חַי־אָנִי is written *As I live*; rule 55 gives the *As* to the predicate adjective as part of the formula's own fixed rendering, the unit discontinuous around the pronoun and headed on *live*.
Explicit pronoun takes only its own *I* (rules 20, 55).
נְאֻם rendered by the finite *saith*.
No article morpheme stands here, so the supplied *the* belongs to the nominal expression it determines (rule 15).
The 1cs suffix of אֲדֹנָי is not separately rendered (rule 22).
Divine name → *Jehovah*.
The oath אִם carries the negative force, and rule 14's correlative clause gives the opening *neither* to the morpheme that is itself what that word says, leaving the closing connective to the waw.
Object noun → *sons*.
Waw takes the closing correlative *nor* (rule 14); a connective the ASV has written for a waw is never added.
The repeated oath אִם before בָּנוֹת is rendered once in English; the repetition goes unrepresented under rule 22, as a repeated בֵּין does in rule 26.
Second object noun → *daughters*.
Finite verb with its English subject pronoun and modal auxiliary (rule 17), headed on the lexical verb.
Explicit pronoun הֵמָּה takes *they*.

לְבַדָּם is rendered by the single English word *only*; rule 30's one-English-word condition is met and no morpheme owns a part of it, so preposition, noun and suffix share one unit headed on the lexeme בַּד. The competing reading would give the suffix its own pronoun, but the ASV's *they* answers to the written הֵמָּה, leaving nothing for the suffix here.
Niphal finite verb with its supplied modal and passive auxiliary, headed on the lexical predicate (rules 17, 24).
Waw rendered by the adversative *but* (rule 14).
Article takes the written *the* (rule 15).
Noun → *land*.
הָיָה as an ordinary copular verb with its supplied modal; headed on *be*.
Predicate noun שְׁמָמָה rendered adjectivally as *desolate*.

review_notes: Corrected: בְּתוֹכָהּ → *were in it* now fuses בְּ+תוֹךְ to *were in* under rule 30 (headed on תָּוֶךְ, the copula joining under rule 49), replacing the accepted split that left תָּוֶךְ `unrepresented`.
Both articles on *these men* go unrepresented: the ASV writes a single determiner for the phrase and the written demonstrative pronoun licenses it (rule 41's limit).
The oath's אִם … וְאִם is read as the source of *neither … nor*, with the first אִם taking *neither*, the waw the *nor*, and the second אִם unrepresented under rule 22.
*though* at the head of the verse is `added`: the protasis opens with the bare numeral and has no conjunction morpheme in it (rule 55).
